verdict_text: YES. The regex fullmatches exactly the 112 per-layer projection weights (7 names × 16 layers), casts them with `.to(torch.bfloat16)` (round-to-nearest-even), and leaves every other tensor float32 with unchanged values since the input is already float32. The buffer pattern `(?!)` never matches, so nothing is deleted; names are preserved; the four required asserts run before writing; and the output goes to `out/T3` via `save_sharded_safetensors` with a 268,435,456-byte cap, which is the required shard limit.
